name: gh-pages

on:
  push:
    branches: ["master"]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: "docs-gh-pages"
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' || !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip docs]') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout master
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: master
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y pandoc
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install pyyaml
          npm install
      - name: Verify Documentating contract
        run: npm test

      - name: Build canonical Antora source tree
        run: |
          python3 tools/build_antora_site.py

      - name: Build site with Antora
        run: |
          npx antora antora-playbook.yml --fetch

      - name: Copy public site extras
        run: |
          if [ -f docs/CNAME ]; then
            cp docs/CNAME .site_build/CNAME
          fi

          if [ -d assets ]; then
            mkdir -p .site_build/assets
            cp -R assets/. .site_build/assets/
          fi

          if [ -d docs/quality-atlas ]; then
            mkdir -p .site_build/quality-atlas
            cp -R docs/quality-atlas/. .site_build/quality-atlas/
          fi

          if [ -d docs/qa-rc ]; then
            mkdir -p .site_build/qa-rc
            cp -R docs/qa-rc/. .site_build/qa-rc/
          fi

          touch .site_build/.nojekyll

      - name: Publish owner-facing site to gh-pages
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git remote set-url origin "https://x-access-token:${GITHUB_TOKEN}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"

          workdir="$(mktemp -d)"

          if git ls-remote --exit-code origin gh-pages >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            git fetch origin gh-pages:gh-pages
            git worktree add --force "$workdir" gh-pages
          else
            git worktree add --detach "$workdir"
            (
              cd "$workdir"
              git checkout --orphan gh-pages
            )
          fi

          find "$workdir" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name '.git' -exec rm -rf {} +
          cp -R .site_build/. "$workdir"/

          (
            cd "$workdir"
            git add -A
            if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
              git commit -m "docs: publish canonical Antora site"
              git push origin HEAD:gh-pages --force
            else
              echo "No site changes to publish."
            fi
          )

          git worktree remove "$workdir" --force || true

          - responses
        default: auto

    - cron: '27 9 */2 * *'

permissions:
  contents: write

  group: quality-atlas-assessment
  cancel-in-progress: false

verdict.summary: Documentating is a mature documentation and publication repository with a clearly automated Antora build path, deterministic content verification, GitHub Pages deployment, and an integrated Quality Atlas workflow; its main readiness gaps are the very large dirty working tree, absence of tagged releases, and limited evidence for external market validation or deeper non-content runtime testing.
strengths: Canonical Antora source and generated publication structure are both present.
Content verification is exposed through npm test and enforced in the GitHub Pages workflow.
GitHub Pages publication is fully automated from verification through Antora build and deployment.
Quality Atlas assessment has its own scheduled and manually dispatchable workflow.
Repository contains explicit governance, gate, deployment, release, smoke, and orchestration support directories.
risks: The working tree contains a very large set of modified and untracked files, reducing release-state clarity.
No exact Git tag is present at the assessed commit, so release provenance is weaker than the build automation.
The supplied evidence demonstrates content-contract verification but not broad behavioral or end-to-end test depth.
External adoption, audience traction, or market validation is not evidenced by the supplied repository facts.
next_actions: Reconcile the current modified and untracked files into intentional commits or generated-artifact cleanup so the repository returns to a reviewable clean baseline.
Introduce an explicit tagged release policy for publication milestones.
Add or evidence end-to-end validation of the generated site beyond the current content-contract verification.
Document measurable publication consumers or adoption signals if market maturity is intended to be scored above internal-platform readiness.
notes: Assessment is based only on the deterministic repository facts and excerpts embedded in the authoritative prompt.
The repository is documentation-centric, so runtime scoring reflects build and publication execution rather than a long-running application service.
No PHP application manifest or PHPUnit/PHPStan configuration is present; this is not treated as a defect because the evidenced implementation is Node, Python, and Antora based.

product.summary: Documentating has a clear product identity as a canonical documentation and publication system built around Antora, with explicit content verification and owner-facing publication workflows.
risks: External user adoption or audience traction is not evidenced in the supplied facts.
improvements: Add measurable publication-consumer or audience evidence if product maturity is intended to include external validation.

architecture.summary: The repository shows strong architectural separation between canonical content, build tooling, governance, deployment, release, smoke, and generated-site concerns.
risks: A very large dirty working tree obscures the distinction between intentional source changes and generated or pending state.
improvements: Restore a clean baseline and keep generated-state ownership explicit so architectural boundaries remain auditable.

runtime.summary: Runtime maturity is solid for a documentation system: the repository defines reproducible verification, canonical-site generation, Antora rendering, and static publication rather than a persistent application runtime.
risks: The supplied evidence does not demonstrate performance, failure-mode, or recovery testing of the publication pipeline.
improvements: Add explicit smoke or end-to-end checks against the generated site and publication result.

qa.summary: Quality assurance is well established through a deterministic content-contract test invoked by npm test and enforced before the canonical Antora build in CI.
risks: Evidence is concentrated on content-contract verification and does not establish broad behavioral or browser-level test coverage.
improvements: Extend verification with generated-site integrity and end-to-end publication checks.

ops.summary: Operational maturity is strong, with automated GitHub Pages deployment, concurrency controls, explicit dependency setup, scheduled Quality Atlas assessment, and dedicated deployment and release structures.
risks: The assessed commit has no exact Git tag and the working tree is heavily modified, weakening operational release traceability.
improvements: Adopt tagged publication milestones and reconcile the dirty tree before release-candidate assertions.

market.summary: The repository demonstrates a coherent internal and owner-facing documentation product, but the supplied facts do not establish external demand, adoption, or competitive market validation.
risks: Market alignment above internal ecosystem utility would be speculative without usage or audience evidence.
improvements: Capture readership, downstream consumers, integrations, or other measurable adoption indicators.

overall.summary: Documentating is a solid-to-strong release candidate for its documentation-platform role, with mature build, verification, publication, and assessment automation; release hygiene and broader validation evidence are the main remaining constraints.
risks: Large uncommitted repository state and missing release tags reduce confidence in a reproducible release baseline.
Testing evidence remains narrower than the otherwise mature build and operations footprint.
improvements: Normalize the working tree, establish tagged releases, and add end-to-end generated-site validation.
